turns.t: Hi Jess, I'm Dana, the nurse. I did your urine dip when you came in, and I'll pass that to the doctor.
Lovely. It's my fourth in six months, so I probably know what it'll say. ~
Hello Jess. It's the urine infections again. Tell me what's different this time.
The usual, burning when I pee, going all the time, and a dull ache low down. It started on Monday.
The dip showed leucocytes and nitrites, doctor, both positive.
Thanks, Dana. Jess, any fever, back pain, or blood in the urine?
No fever. No back pain. A tiny bit of blood, I think, yesterday.
Any discharge or new partner? ~
No, nothing like that. ~
What do you drink, how much fluid in a day?
About a litre, I think. Mostly coffee, to be honest.
That's not a lot. And do you hold on when you need to go? ~
At work, yes. I'm a teacher, and it's hard to get away. ~
Let me press on your tummy. ~
Okay.
A little tender over the bladder, and no tenderness over the kidneys.
What does that mean? ~
It fits with a bladder infection again. But with four in six months, I can't rule out something that makes you prone to them, like a stone, or a problem with emptying the bladder.
Oh. Right. ~
I'd like to send a urine sample off to the lab, to grow the germ and see which antibiotic works.
I can send that off now, doctor. ~
And I'd like to arrange a kidney and bladder ultrasound, to look for a cause.
Will that tell you something? ~
It will show whether the bladder empties fully, and whether there are stones. ~
Right. And treatment? ~
I'll write that up when the lab has answered, because I want to choose the right drug, so drink plenty of water now, and a glass every hour.
I can try. ~
Empty your bladder fully, wipe front to back, and go as soon as you need to, even at work.
I'll tell my head. ~
If you get a fever, shaking, or back pain, come in the same day, because that could mean the kidneys.
I will. Thanks, both. ~
